summary: deploy.sh runs migrations as postgres — new tables locked away from runtime guru role
description:
deploy/deploy.sh:68 currently runs each migration as the `postgres` superuser:

  sudo -u postgres /usr/bin/psql -d guru -1 -f "$f"

So every CREATE TABLE produces a table owned by `postgres`. The runtime app connects as `guru` (DATABASE_URL) and has no implicit access to postgres-owned tables in PG 17 — exactly the regression that surfaced as `permission denied for table users` (42501) on /api/quota, /api/sessions, /api/query.

Prod was unblocked by granting `guru` SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on existing tables and setting ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES so future postgres-created tables auto-grant to guru. That works but is a workaround — the architecturally correct fix is for the migration role to BE the runtime role, so tables are owned by `guru` from creation and future ALTER TABLE migrations need no privilege gymnastics.

Fix:
- Pipe `SET ROLE guru;` into psql before each migration body, still using `sudo -u postgres ... -1` so the whole thing is one transaction. Tables created in that session are owned by guru.
- Update the comment block above the loop to explain why.

Prerequisites (verify before merging):
- `guru` must have CREATE on schema public. Database is `CREATE DATABASE guru OWNER guru`, so `pg_database_owner` membership normally grants this in PG 15+, but verify on prod with:
    sudo -u postgres psql -d guru -c "SELECT has_schema_privilege('guru','public','CREATE')"
  If false: `GRANT CREATE ON SCHEMA public TO guru;` (one-time prod op, not in the migration files since this is a permissions setup concern).

Out-of-band cleanup (one-time, not part of this PR):
- Existing tables stay owned by `postgres`. They have GRANTs now so SELECT/INSERT etc. work, but only `postgres` can ALTER/DROP them. To make future schema migrations clean, transfer ownership:
    ALTER TABLE users OWNER TO guru;  (and the other 5 app tables)
  Defer until needed — pure GRANT works for the current schema.

Out of scope:
- Corpus tables (chunks, traditions, etc.) are populated by guru-pipeline's pg_restore, separate concern.
- Webhook signing/replay (already covered by Stripe/Clerk).

No test (this is a deploy-script change verified by the next prod deploy succeeding and `\dt` showing `Owner=guru` for the next-created table).

resolution.note: deploy.sh now SETs ROLE guru in the same -1 transaction so future migrations create tables owned by the runtime role. Verify guru has CREATE on schema public before merging (one-time GRANT if not). Existing tables still owned by postgres — workaround GRANTs cover them; ownership transfer left as a separate op.
